We're building a shared AI platform that powers the next generation of our product portfolio - multi-agent orchestration, ML scoring infrastructure, and LLM-powered intelligence products. As Principal AI Engineer, you'll architect this platform, set the technical direction, and define the engineering standards that the organization builds against. 

This is a hands-on technical leadership role - not a management position. You set architectural direction and write production code every day. You think in ADRs, trade-off matrices, and failure modes. You use Claude Code and AI accelerators to operate at 3-5x speed, and you teach the team to do the same. 

Your work directly shapes a growing AI product portfolio. The platform you architect becomes the shared foundation - every subsequent product launches faster because of the infrastructure decisions you make now. 

You'll be based in India, working hybrid (3 days in-office per week), and will report to the VP of Engineering / CTO. 

What You'll Do

Own AI Platform Architecture : 

- Design the full AI platform - multi-agent orchestration, ML inference infrastructure, LLM gateway, tool registry, and eval/observability stack
 - Write Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) that the organization builds against
 - Make build-vs-buy decisions, evaluate emerging frameworks (A2A, MCP, Visa TAP), and define integration patterns
 - Design system-level concerns: auth gating, policy enforcement (OPA), API gateway patterns (Kong), and multi-tenant isolation
 - Define reference architectures for AI-enabled services across . NET 10 APIs, Python ML workloads, React frontends, AKS deployments, Kong gateway integration, and Azure DevOps delivery pipelines

Drive Product AI Strategy : 

- Partner with Product and CTO office to translate business objectives into AI technical strategy
 - Identify where AI creates differentiated value - predictive models, conversational agents, intelligent automation
 - Evaluate and de-risk emerging technologies. Present to executive leadership on AI capabilities, costs, and competitive positioning
 - Define the AI FinOps strategy: token metering, model routing for cost optimization, quota management, and budget forecasting
 - Establish clear platform decision rules for when AI capabilities should be implemented as . NET services, Python services, Azure ML pipelines, background jobs, or embedded product workflows

AI Safety, Governance And Responsible AI : 

- Define and enforce the Responsible AI framework - content safety guardrails, PII governance, bias testing, and audit trails
 - Ensure all AI systems meet PCI DSS, SOC 2, and emerging AI regulation requirements
 - Establish model validation and governance processes - transparency, explainability, and fairness are non-negotiable
 - Build the trust infrastructure that enables the organization to deploy AI confidently in regulated financial services
 - Champion ethical AI principles; ensure all agents and models comply with global financial regulations and internal compliance standards

Write Code - Everyday : 

- Write production code, review critical PRs, debug complex agent interactions, and prototype new capabilities
 - Lead by example - your code quality, testing discipline, and documentation set the standard
 - Use Claude Code and AI accelerators daily. Build custom skills, MCP integrations, and automation workflows

Mentor And Multiply The Team : 

- Raise the AI engineering bar across the organization. Run design reviews, pair on complex problems
 - Champion AI-accelerated development - train the team on Claude Code workflows, custom skills, and agentic tooling
 - Define engineering standards, evaluation criteria, and best practices that scale beyond your direct team

Must-Have Qualifications

- 10+ years in software engineering with 5+ years in AI/ML - you've architected and shipped production AI systems
 - System design mastery - multi-agent architectures, ML platforms, or large-scale inference systems
 - Azure + Microsoft AI stack deep expertise - Azure ML, AI Foundry, Semantic Kernel, . NET agent frameworks
 - Python + . NET bilingual - Python for ML/data, . NET/C# for agent runtimes
 - LLM systems at production scale - prompt management, RAG, content safety, agentic workflows
 - AI-first development velocity - Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent at 3-5x speed
 - Deep experience architecting modern . NET cloud-native platforms - including API-first service design, distributed systems, Kubernetes deployment, gateway integration, and CI/CD governance

Nice-to-Have

- FinTech / Payments architecture - PCI DSS, SOC 2, regulated AI
 - Agentic Commerce & A2A - Google A2A, MCP, Visa TAP
 - Technical leadership track record - mentored teams, ADR processes, C-level presentations
 - Omnichannel & voice AI - web chat, voice, SMS, Azure Communication Services
 - ML platform engineering - model registries, feature stores, drift detection
 - Published or open-source contributions in AI/ML

Education

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, AI/ML, Mathematics, or a related technical field required. A Master's degree is preferred - but we value what you've built and the systems you've architected over credentials.

Description

Selling Partner Identity Verification (SPIV) ensures that Amazon is a safe and trustworthy place to shop and an amazing place to build a successful business selling products. Our mission is to build trust with our Customers and Selling Partners as we scale through technology, analytics, and science. We're committed to service as a center of excellence for Amazon. 

As part of SPIV, Seller Verification owns variety of products which enables us to collect data from WW Sellers in order to let them sell on Amazon marketplace. Our mission is to: (a) make it simple and fast for Sellers to register globally, (b) verify the identity of every person and business selling on Amazon through the Seller lifecycle, and (c) use automation to achieve accuracy, speed, and scale. When we are successful, we enable Marketplace growth and build trust with our Customers. Registration Systems receive ~1. 5M hits per week and strive towards providing a seamless experience that cannot be exploited by bad actors. As of today, sellers who intend to go global on Amazon need to register in each region and thus, go through the tedious registration process multiple times, which leads to friction for potential global sellers. 

We are looking for a Software Development Manager with a strong sense of ownership and a passion for delivering creative solutions for complex problems on an unprecedented scale. As part of leading a team of engineers, you will have the opportunity to create significant impact on our systems, our business and most importantly, our customers as we take on challenges that can reshape the e-commerce industry. 

We are seeking someone who has strong technical, project and people skills with a can-do attitude and a focus on delivering high quality software. We move at a fast pace and deliver software iteratively using AGILE best practices and the latest technologies. 

The Ideal Candidate

data.title: Global IT Quality Engineer Manager
data.description:
Who We Are

Boston Consulting Group partners with leaders in business and society to tackle their most important challenges and capture their greatest opportunities. BCG was the pioneer in business strategy when it was founded in 1963. Today, we help clients with total transformation-inspiring complex change, enabling organizations to grow, building competitive advantage, and driving bottom-line impact. 

To succeed, organizations must blend digital and human capabilities. Our diverse, global teams bring deep industry and functional expertise and a range of perspectives to spark change. BCG delivers solutions through leading-edge management consulting along with technology and design, corporate and digital ventures-and business purpose. We work in a uniquely collaborative model across the firm and throughout all levels of the client organization, generating results that allow our clients to thrive. 

What You'll Do

The People Digital Product Portfolio is the largest and most dynamic product portfolio within BCG's Digital Products Organization. We enable global technology for BCG's People Function, including Recruiting; Talent Management (Staffing, Mobility & Career Development); L&D; and Core HR (including Workday, Compensation and Benefits). 

We are seeking a Global Quality Engineer Manager to lead quality engineering execution for our Vendor Management System (VMS) products. This is a hands-on technical leadership role focused on ensuring the quality, reliability, and scalability of enterprise SaaS applications through effective manual and automated testing. 

You Will

- Lead and mentor quality engineers across manual and automated testing, providing technical guidance, coaching, and quality oversight. 
 - Develop and execute test strategies for the VMS product/platform, aligned with established quality engineering standards. 
 - Remain hands-on with test automation, contributing to framework development, implementation, and code reviews. 
 - Drive automation initiatives to improve test coverage, efficiency, reliability, and release confidence. 
 - Ensure comprehensive testing of VMS workflows, business rules, APIs, integrations, databases, and backend services. 
 - Partner with product owners, business analysts, and engineers to translate requirements into effective test scenarios, including negative, boundary, integration, and edge cases. 
 - Collaborate with development and DevOps teams to integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines and enable continuous testing. 
 - Lead defect triage and root cause analysis for complex or recurring issues and work with engineering teams on preventive actions. 
 - Track and report quality metrics, including defect trends, test coverage, automation coverage, and defect leakage, to identify risks and improvement opportunities. 
 - Provide quality assessments and recommendations to support release readiness and release decisions. 
 - Recommend and adopt appropriate testing tools and technologies to improve quality engineering effectiveness. 
 - Drive adoption of established QA practices and foster a quality-first culture within the VMS team. 

What You'll Bring

Required Experience

- 8+ years of experience in Software Quality Assurance / Quality Engineering, with expertise in both manual and automation testing. 
 - Experience leading or technically guiding QA/Quality Engineering teams and mentoring engineers. 
 - Strong hands-on experience developing and maintaining automated test suites and frameworks. 
 - Experience testing SaaS-based enterprise products, preferably multi-tenant and cloud-native applications. 
 - Experience testing workflow-driven enterprise platforms such as Vendor Management, Procurement, Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM), HR, or similar business applications. 
 - Experience across functional, integration, regression, API, UI, end-to-end, and data validation testing. 
 - Experience working with APIs, databases, backend services, and enterprise system integrations. 
 - Experience integrating automated testing into CI/CD pipelines. 
 - Experience working in Agile/Scrum environments with globally distributed, cross-functional teams. 

Preferred Experience

- Experience testing SaaS-based Vendor Management or Procurement platforms such as SAP Fieldglass, Coupa, or similar enterprise workflow applications. 
 - Experience with performance and load testing. 
 - Exposure to AI-enabled testing tools or applications of AI within Quality Engineering. 

Key Skills

- Strong understanding of QA methodologies, SDLC, STLC, Agile testing practices, and Quality Engineering principles. 
 - Hands-on expertise with Playwright (preferred) or Selenium. 
 - Experience with automation approaches such as Page Object Model (POM), Hybrid, and Data-Driven frameworks. 
 - Proficiency in Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, or Python for automation scripting. 
 - Experience with API testing using Postman; knowledge of REST Assured or similar frameworks is an advantage. 
 - Experience with test and defect management tools such as JIRA, Zephyr, and QMetry. 
 - Experience with Git and CI/CD tools such as Jenkins, GitHub Actions, or equivalent technologies. 
 - Strong understanding of enterprise SaaS applications, APIs, integrations, databases, and workflow-driven systems. 
 - Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving capabilities. 

Who You'll Work With

You'll work with a globally distributed, cross-functional team of product owners, business analysts, software engineers, DevOps engineers, architects, quality engineers, and business stakeholders in a fast-paced Agile environment. 

As a hands-on technical quality leader, you will mentor quality engineers and partner with product and engineering teams to ensure quality is embedded throughout the development lifecycle

Additional info

You're Good At

Technical Leadership

- Providing clear technical direction while remaining hands-on when needed. 
 - Coaching and developing quality engineers. 
 - Raising engineering standards through constructive reviews and knowledge sharing. 

Problem Solving & Decision Making

- Anticipating risks and identifying issues early. 
 - Making pragmatic, risk-based decisions while balancing quality, timelines, and business priorities. 
 - Navigating complex technical and business problems with sound judgment. 

Communication & Collaboration

- Communicating clearly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. 
 - Influencing teams and building alignment across functions and geographies. 
 - Giving and receiving constructive feedback effectively. 

Work Management & Organization

- Managing multiple priorities in a dynamic environment. 
 - Demonstrating strong attention to detail while maintaining focus on broader outcomes. 
 - Taking ownership and driving work through to completion. 

Customer & Business Focus

- Understanding business workflows and the impact of product quality on users. 
 - Balancing technical quality with business needs and user experience. 
 - Maintaining a strong focus on reliable and scalable product outcomes. 

Continuous Improvement

- Challenging existing ways of working and identifying practical opportunities for improvement. 
 - Staying current with evolving quality engineering technologies and practices. 
 - Promoting learning, experimentation, and continuous improvement within the team. 

Values & Ethics

- Demonstrating accountability, sound judgment, and integrity. 
 - Handling confidential business and user information appropriately. 

At BCG, our people and relationships are at the heart of everything we do. We believe that in-person collaboration plays an important role in our culture, mentorship, and professional development. 

For this role, you will generally be expected to work from a BCG office or in person with clients on a regular basis (typically around 50% of working time), depending on business needs and in line with local policies and practices. 

We aim to provide a dynamic and collaborative environment that fosters connection and teamwork.

Job Title: Director - Quality Assurance

Solution Line: Aon Business Services

Team: Quality and Business Excellence

Position Type: Full Time

Work Mode: Hybrid

Cab Facility: Yes

Shift Time: 12: 00 PM - 9: 00 PM (IST)

People Manager Role: Yes

Work Experience

- 25+ years of experience, including 15+ years leading Quality, Controls, or Assurance functions in a GCC/shared services environment. 
 - Experience managing operational quality, controls, and SLA/KPI performance. 
 - Strong exposure to international stakeholders and cross-functional operations. 
 - Lean Six Sigma Black Belt (mandatory). 

Technical Skills

- Quality assurance and control framework design. 
 - QA/QC sampling methodologies and error taxonomy development. 
 - SLA/KPI definition, monitoring, and benchmarking. 
 - Dashboarding, executive reporting, and governance. 
 - Root cause analysis and continuous improvement. 

Behavioral Skills

- Executive presence and credibility with senior onshore, Risk, Compliance, and Internal Audit stakeholders
 - Independence and the courage to escalate control failures and hold the line on standards
 - Strong people leadership - able to build, coach, and retain a specialist team from a standing start
 - Pragmatism in balancing control rigor with operational throughput and transition timelines
 - Clarity in communicating control and quality expectations across sites and cultures (e. g. , India, Poland)

Job Overview

The Quality & Control Leader will establish and lead the Quality & Control function as a key pillar within Aon's Global Capability Centers (GCCs). This role will design, implement, and govern the operational quality and control framework across GCC operations, ensuring robust process controls, consistent quality standards, and effective assurance mechanisms. 

The incumbent will be responsible for creating a culture of quality excellence by defining operational control standards, implementing quality assurance methodologies, and providing leadership visibility through governance and reporting. The role will partner closely with operational teams, Business Excellence, and Transition teams to ensure new services and processes are launched with strong controls from day one. 

Core Responsibilities

- Design, implement, and continuously enhance the GCC-wide Quality & Control Framework, including quality standards, assurance methodologies, control testing approaches, and governance requirements. 
 - Establish and oversee QA/QC processes, including sampling methodologies, quality scorecards, error taxonomy, defect classification, root cause analysis, and corrective action management across all GCC operations. 
 - Monitor control effectiveness and quality performance, ensuring operational teams consistently meet established SLAs, KPIs, compliance requirements, and client expectations. 
 - Develop and lead governance forums through robust dashboards, executive reporting, issue tracking, and escalation mechanisms, providing GCC leadership with visibility into quality and control performance. 
 - Drive continuous improvement initiatives by identifying process gaps, recurring defects, and operational risks, and implementing sustainable solutions to improve accuracy, efficiency, and customer outcomes. 
 - Partner closely with Business Excellence, Transition, and Operations leaders to embed quality and control requirements into due diligence, process design, and go-live readiness activities, ensuring new workstreams are operationally controlled from inception. 
 - Benchmark quality and operational performance against industry standards and best practices, recommending enhancements to strengthen GCC delivery maturity and stakeholder confidence. 
 - Lead, coach, and develop a team of quality and control professionals, fostering a culture of accountability, operational excellence, and continuous learning. 
 - Act as the independent control authority within the GCC, challenging ineffective practices, escalating significant control failures, and driving timely remediation of identified risks and defects. 
 - Build strong relationships with global stakeholders, ensuring alignment on quality expectations, governance requirements, and continuous improvement priorities across regions and functions. 

How We Support Our Colleagues

In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we are proud to be an equal opportunity workforce. At Aon, we believe a diverse workforce is an innovative workforce. Our agile, inclusive environment allows colleagues to manage their wellbeing and work/life balance while empowering you to be your authentic self. 

Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two "Global Wellbeing Days" each year, encouraging them to take time to focus on themselves. We offer a variety of workstyle options through our Smart Working model, but we also recognize that flexibility goes beyond just the place of work. . . and we are all for it!

Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips colleagues to learn, share and grow, helping them achieve their fullest potential. As a result, Aon colleagues are more connected, more relevant and more valued.

Position: Controls Engineer

Experience: 5-7 Years

Industry: EV Motor & Inverter Manufacturing

Location: Pune / Manufacturing Plant Environment

Function: Maintenance / Industrial Automation

The Controls Engineer will be responsible for automation systems, machine controls, testing stations, safety systems, and commissioning of equipment used in EV motor & inverter manufacturing and testing. The role involves close coordination with production, maintenance, quality, and OEM suppliers to ensure robust, safe, and optimized control systems.

 - Troubleshoot machine communication networks, field buses, and I/O diagnostics; ensure electrical schematics and logic documentation are current. 
 - Drive poka‐yoke, interlocks, vision systems, DC tools and traceability enhancements to improve first pass yield and reduce rework. 
 - Integrate sensors, actuators, drives, servo systems, and VFDs used in inverter and motor production. 
 - Work with industrial communication protocols such as: 
 - Profinet / Profibus / EtherNet‐IP / Modbus / CAN
 - Support data acquisition for SCADA / MES / traceability systems. 
 - Enable machine connectivity and basic Industry 4. 0 initiatives. 

Education And Qualifications

- BE / BTech in Electrical, Electronics, Instrumentation, Mechatronics
 - Certified PLC training
 - Experience in EV / Automotive / Power Electronics manufacturing
 - Knowledge of traction inverter or motor test systems is a strong advantage
 - Exposure to lean manufacturing and TPM concepts

Skills and Competencies

Technical Skills Required

- PLC Platforms: Siemens (S7-1200/1500), Allen‐Bradley, Mitsubishi
 - HMI/SCADA: TIA Portal, WinCC, FactoryTalk, Ignition

data.title: Senior Quality Engineer
data.description:
About StarRez

StarRez is the global leader in student housing software, providing innovative solutions for on and off-campus housing management, resident wellness and experience, and revenue generation. Trusted by 1, 400+ clients across 25+ countries, StarRez supports more than 4 million beds annually with its user-friendly, all-in-one platform, delivering seamless experiences for students and administrators. With offices in the United States, Australia, the UK, and India, StarRez blends the robust capabilities of a global organization with the personalized care and service of a trusted partner. 

Role: 

As a Senior Quality Engineer - you will play a pivotal role in elevating our quality practices across customer-facing event management workflows, booking and registration experiences, operational administration, product integrations, and complex distributed systems. You will be an expert within our engineering organization, deeply understanding product behaviour, customer journeys, business rules, and the systems that support seamless conference and event experiences. This role will balance hands-on individual contributor responsibilities with leading, influencing, and coaching your peers. 

This individual contributor role is for someone who is passionate about seeing systems holistically, has a strong vision for product quality, and is eager to drive the highest standards of customer experience, functional correctness, usability, accessibility, reliability, performance, and release confidence. You will leverage your deep understanding of SaaS product behaviour, end-to-end workflows, integrations, environments, and customer operations to guide and influence our development process. 

You will not manage people. You will set the quality bar for your team, do the work to hold it, and coach the engineers, product managers and designers around you to share ownership of it. You will report to the Director of Quality and work day-to-day with your team's Engineering Manager, Product Manager and engineers, alongside Support and Implementation Services when payment issues reach customers. 

What You Will Own: 

- Own the end-to-end test strategy within your team's area, deciding how things get tested based on the risk each change carries. 
 - Design validation for payment flows including authorisation, capture, settlement, partial and full refunds, failed and retried transactions, chargebacks, idempotency, and reconciliation between our records and the provider's. 
 - Coach and support your team to make of quality everyone's responsibility, and provide hands on support via executing testing activities when required. 
 - Validate integrations with third party payment gateways and providers. 
 - Engage from discovery and refinement onward: challenge assumptions, surface missing scenarios, and make sure acceptance criteria are specific and testable before a story is picked up. 
 - Assess your team's current quality maturity honestly, build a plan to lift it over the next two to three quarters, and share what you learn with Senior QAs on other teams facing the same gaps. 
 - Coach engineers on testing principles, test design, and shared ownership of automated tests, the goal is a team that builds quality in, not a QA who inspects for it. 
 - Mentor mid-level QA engineers on risk assessment, automation, observability and shift left practice. 
 - Contribute to CI/CD pipeline health and deployment quality gates: test suite selection, environment readiness, pre and post deploy checks, and safe release strategies including feature flags and staged rollout. 
 - Own production defect triage for Payments: assess customer and financial impact, distinguish severity from priority, drive fixes at the right urgency, follow through to root cause & prevention, and provide regular updates on defect remediation. 
 - Represent Payments quality in incident reviews and, where needed, in conversations with Support and customer facing teams. 

Required Qualifications: 

- 5+ years of progressive software engineering or quality engineering with deep focus on quality in complex, distributed system environments 
 - Hands-on experience collaborating with cross-functional teams to translate customer needs into well-defined user stories, acceptance criteria, and risk-based test scenarios that support high-quality product delivery. 
 - Proven track record advocating for quality and ability to influence technical direction through innovative, pragmatic, and evidence-based approaches. 
 - Hands-on experience working with web-based products, including front-end behaviour, API, service integration and functional end-to-end testing. 
 - Experience contributing to test automation frameworks and using and have a solid understanding of the testing pyramid. 
 - Practical experience working with CI/CD pipelines using GitHub, Build-kite, or similar platforms. 
 - Experience contributing to deployment and release quality gates, including test suite selection and environment readiness checks. 
 - Ability to translate customer needs into well-defined user stories, acceptance criteria, and risk-based test scenarios in collaboration with cross functional teams. 
 - Strong root cause analysis and problem-solving skills across complex, multi system failures. 
 - Excellent technical communication, you influence engineers, product managers and business stakeholders through evidence and expertise rather than authority. 
 - Practical experience using AI in modern software development, with sound judgement about where it helps and where it does not. 
 - Genuine curiosity about product architecture, customer workflows, and the business impact of engineering decisions. 

Reasons to join our team: 

- Opportunity to be a part of a well-established, high-performance company that has been in business for over 30+ years
 - Full benefits including health care, paid time off, and others
 - A supportive team environment with emphasis on learning and development opportunities
 - Our Promise: You will learn, grow, and be appreciated for your impact and contributions. 
 - Z-Factor: Our most celebrated value, you will work with a team of caring, high-performing, and passionate people who have fun supporting our vision, innovation, and continuous improvement. 

Even if you don't have all of the Qualifications listed above, but feel you have what it takes to succeed in the role, we would love to hear from you!

StarRez is an equal opportunity employer.

data.description:
Xplor Technologies powers the experiences at the heart of everyday life. Through modern vertical software, embedded payments, and AI-powered capabilities, we help businesses in fitness, recreation, golf and club, field services, laundry, education, and other membership-based and service-based industries simplify operations, uncover insights, and elevate customer and member experiences. 

Job Description

About the opportunity

Join our Embedded Payments team as a DevOps Engineer to make a real impact every day. We say that because we know that every conversation we have, every pipeline we build and every system we automate is another opportunity for us to elevate everyday life experiences for our customers and the people and communities they serve. 

Reporting into the DevOps Engineering Manager, you'll help us build and scale the infrastructure behind our cloud-native payment orchestration platform that processes significant transaction volume across multiple Xplor brands. You are passionate about building reliable, secure systems and the automation that keeps them running smoothly while maintaining engineering best practices. You think about infrastructure end-to-end, from CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure as code down to monitoring, alerting, and incident response. You're comfortable owning the platform that everything runs on and collaborating closely with backend, frontend, QA, and engineering teams to ship and operate high-quality software. 

Our Tech Stack

- Cloud: AWS (ECS, Lambda, RDS/Aurora PostgreSQL, API Gateway, SQS, EventBridge, Cognito, KMS, VPC) 
 - Infrastructure as Code: Terraform 
 - CI/CD: Bitbucket Pipelines 
 - Observability: SigNoz, Grafana, CloudWatch 
 - Performance & Load Testing: k6 
 - Security & Compliance: PCI DSS, AWS-native controls 
 - Application stack supported: Node. js services, React frontends Responsibilities & Duties

- Design, build, and maintain AWS infrastructure using Terraform, with attention to scalability, cost, and PCI-scoped network segmentation 
 - Own and evolve the observability stack - SigNoz for distributed tracing and metrics, Grafana for dashboards, structured logging - so engineers can answer "what's happening in production" without paging you 
 - Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines in Bitbucket Pipelines, including deployment guardrails, automated rollback strategies, and environment promotion workflows 
 - Design and run performance and load tests with k6 or other custom tools as needed, establish baseline benchmarks, and partner with engineering to address bottlenecks before they reach production 
 - Participate in on-call rotations, lead incident response for infrastructure issues, and drive postmortems that produce durable fixes 
 - Define and track SLOs, error budgets, and operational KPIs for payment-critical services 
 - Improve deployment velocity and safety - faster pipelines, better preview environments, safer migration tooling 
 - Partner with security and compliance to maintain PCI DSS posture, support audits (Armanino/Vanta), and codify controls 
 - Manage cost and capacity across AWS - right-sizing, reserved capacity strategy, and identifying optimization opportunities 
 - Use AI-assisted tools effectively to accelerate infrastructure work without compromising review quality or security posture

Qualifications

What would make me a good candidate?

We are looking for curious and empathetic people. We also love to hear from people who are motivated by meaningful work, resonate with our core values, have a positive outlook, are comfortable with ambiguity and thrive working in an ever-evolving and complex environment. We are inspired by meeting big-picture thinkers and doers, people who can be both tactical and strategic, aim high and put people first in everything they do. 

You'll need: 

- 5+ years of professional DevOps, SRE, or Platform Engineering experience, with a Computer Science/Engineering degree or equivalent 
 - Strong hands-on AWS experience across compute (ECS, Lambda), networking (VPC, security groups), data (RDS/Aurora), and event-driven services (SQS, EventBridge) 
 - Production Terraform experience - module design, state management, drift handling, and multi-environment patterns 
 - Experience operating an observability stack in production; familiarity with SigNoz, Grafana, or comparable tools (Datadog, New Relic, Prometheus) 
 - Experience designing and running load tests with k6 or comparable tools (JMeter, Gatling, Locust) 
 - Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines (Bitbucket Pipelines, GitHub Actions, CircleCI, or similar) 
 - Strong shell scripting ability or similar in a scripting oriented language (Python, Go, etc. . . ) 
 - Ability to read and understand back end and and front end code in order to implement infrastructure more effectively 
 - Solid understanding of networking fundamentals such as sockets, routing, load balancing, SSL/TLS encryption, tunneling, firewalls/security groups, etc. . . , 
 - Understanding of access control and identity management (IAM, OIDC, Cognito, OAUTH in general or similar) 
 - Comfort leading incident response and writing postmortems that drive systemic improvement 
 - Fluency with AI-assisted development tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, etc. ) and an articulate point of view on where they help and where they don't 
 - Comfortable working on a 100% remote team and operating independently within an agile group It would be great if you also have: 

- Experience operating PCI-compliant or otherwise regulated environments 
 - Experience with payments infrastructure or other high-availability transactional systems 
 - Familiarity with Vanta or comparable compliance automation tooling 
 - Experience tuning PostgreSQL for high-throughput workloads 
 - Exposure to KMS-based cryptography, secrets management, and key rotation strategies 
 - Experience with chaos engineering or game-day exercises At Xplor, we believe that the best innovation and ideas happen at the intersections of our differences - people of diverse cultures, generations, disciplines, and lived experiences. So even if you think you do not tick all the boxes, we still encourage you to apply. 

Additional Information

Values and Life at Xplor

Our five core values guide us from how we hire and recognise our team members to how we interact with our customers day to day: 

- Find a better way
 - Do the right thing
 - Say it straight
 - Win together
 - Own the outcomeIf these values sound like you, and describe people you want to work with, you will thrive at Xplor. 

As an Xplorer, you will be part of a global network of talented colleagues who will support your success. We look for commonalities and shared passions and give people the tools they need to deliver great work and grow at speed. 

Some of our perks and benefits are: 

- Paid Parental Leave benefit programs
 - #GiveBackDays/Commitment to social impact - 3 extra days off to volunteer and give back to your local community
 - Ongoing dedication to Diversity & Inclusion initiatives such as D&I Council, Global Mentorship Program
 - Access to free mental health support
 - Flexible working arrangementsReady to apply?

To start your application, please submit your resume, and we will be in touch as soon as we can. Please include the word "moonshot" at the top of your message to the Hiring Manager so that we know you took the time to read our job ad. 

Before you apply

To be considered for employment, you must be legally authorised to work in India. This applies to remote roles too, as we can only employ people who reside within India. Xplor does not sponsor visas, either at the time of hire or at any later time. We're also not able to offer contractor arrangements or Employer of Record engagements for this position at this stage. 

Please apply through our careers portal or external job boards only. We're unable to upload emailed applications, as our process requires you to answer screening questions directly. 

We also invite you to check out our Candidate FAQs for more information about our recruitment process xplor. com/recruitment-faqs/. 

Interview Recording and Background Checks

As part of our hiring process, successful candidates will be asked to complete background and identity verification checks. Many of our roles are remote, and to protect both candidates and our business from recruitment fraud, we may record video interviews during the process. We keep any recordings and related data only for as long as the hiring process is active and do not retain them afterwards. 

EEO and Artificial Intelligence

We believe in transparent hiring. We use an applicant tracking system with artificial intelligence-enabled features to support our recruitment process, but our recruitment team makes all hiring decisions after human review. We do not rely on artificial intelligence to make final hiring decisions. Find our Candidate AI Usage guidelines here. 

Xplor is committed to providing equal opportunities in employment and creating an inclusive work environment. We provide equal opportunities to all our employees and to all eligible applicants for employment in our company. data.title: Full-Stack Engineer — Systems Conductor
data.description:
About Bold Business

Bold Business is an AI-first, delivery-first company building production-grade enterprise software, automation engines, and autonomous agent infrastructure. We build the way modern teams build: our engineers are not syntax-typists but Systems Conductors, who leverage advanced AI-agent developer environments to design, build, test, and ship production software at multiples of traditional manual velocity. 

The Role

We're hiring Full-Stack Systems Conductors to own feature delivery across our flagship TechForce platform - spanning React/TypeScript frontends, Python/FastAPI backends, and robust PostgreSQL data schemas. 

You'll own high-impact modules from day one, but your true value lies in your ability to design robust databases, orchestrate complex systems, and lead background coding agents through rigorous, test-driven implementations. 

Two principles define how we work, and we hire for both explicitly: 

AI-Agentic Command. AI coding environments (Cursor, Claude Code CLI, OpenClaw / Hermes Agents / Grokbot / other personal agent harnesses, and custom Model Context Protocol servers) are our native workspace, not a novelty. We expect you to command agents to write boilerplate, scaffold routes, and draft test suites. You provide the system architecture, the security guardrails, and the rigorous critical review. Speed from agents, judgment from you. 

Collaborative by Default. Every change is strictly peer-reviewed through pull requests. Documentation and automated unit tests ship in the same PR as the code. Blockers get raised early, not discovered at review. We value highly legible, standardized architectures that outlive their author's immediate attention - brilliant work that only its author understands is a liability here, not an asset. 

What You'll Do

- Architect schema-first features: design strict API boundaries, typed contracts, and database schemas first, providing the structure background AI agents need to implement features safely
 - Build and secure module workflows: own recruiter and admin interfaces (screens, tables, profiles, forms, filters, dashboards), REST endpoints, and PostgreSQL relational workflows - with business security and authorization policies strictly enforced at the data layer
 - Establish codebase context: build and use MCP servers and AST-based dependency graphs to give developer agents standardized, structured access to our repositories
 - Orchestrate quality loops: set up local testing environments and containerized CI/CD checks where background agents automatically execute test runs, linting, and type validation before any merge
 - Engage directly with stakeholders: sit with non-technical stakeholders to translate messy operational processes into clean, executable technical requirements - and keep them in the loop as the work progresses
 - Stabilize and maintain the platform: production defects, small-to-medium gaps, and reporting migration support as Power BI is retired
 - Review and be reviewed: give and receive pull-request review as a normal working rhythm, with test evidence on every ticket

Non-Negotiables

We'll ask you to demonstrate all of the following - come ready with real examples: 

- Active agentic developer loop. You've transitioned beyond copy-pasting code blocks from a browser window. You can walk us through your CLI-native agentic loop: how you coordinate agents, what parameters and guardrails you set, and - specifically - a time you caught and patched an LLM hallucination before it shipped. "I've tried Copilot" is not this. 
 - Collaboration you can prove. A working history of PR reviews given and received, documentation you wrote that someone else actually used, and a time you escalated a blocker early instead of grinding on it alone. We will check for this specifically. 
 - Full-stack competency, production-grade. Strong React/TypeScript and Python/FastAPI experience on real systems in real use - not tutorials or side scripts. 
 - Database schema and security mastery. Highly fluent in PostgreSQL - schema design, migrations, indexing, transactional isolation. You understand why hiding a button in React is not an authorization control; authorization is enforced in the data layer. 
 - Clean systems architecture. You build robust, decoupled state machines (FastAPI, React state, background queues) that gracefully isolate, log, and recover from real-world API and network failures. 
 - Enterprise systems awareness. You've designed, maintained, or operated within ERP-class platforms (SAP, Oracle, Workday, NetSuite, or comparable) - or can clearly demonstrate how they work and why they matter: integrated data, standardized process, and a single operational source of truth. You'll help build a platform that plays exactly this role, so you need to understand what it replaces and what it must not break. 
 - True Agile and continuous improvement. Not standup theater - iterative delivery, working software shipped in small increments, retrospectives that actually change how the team works. Come ready to describe a real process improvement you drove based on what a sprint or a failure taught you. 
 - End-to-end micro-project ownership. You'll run micro-projects through their full lifecycle: planning and requirements gathering with stakeholders, implementation, testing, and maintenance afterward - documenting your work and processes clearly enough that another team member can be trained to support and back up what you built without you in the room. Come ready to walk us through one project you carried from first conversation to steady-state maintenance. 
 - Strong English communication, written and spoken. You'll operate in a U. S. -based team environment and explain technical decisions to non-technical stakeholders. 

Nice to Have

- Hands-on experience with OpenClaw, Hermes Agents, or Grokbot agent platforms
 - Familiarity with LangGraph or stateful multi-agent orchestration
 - Operations-heavy SaaS experience (recruiting, workforce management, ATS, or CRM)
 - Multi-tenant application experience
 - AWS exposure (EC2, RDS, S3, cloud logs)
 - Data imports, deduplication, search/filter interfaces, operational reporting
 - Experience joining a codebase mid-flight and getting productive fast

What This Role Is

- A hands-on builder-conductor role with defined module ownership
 - AI-accelerated delivery with human judgment on every merge
 - A high-performing team operating model: review, documentation, and early communication are the job, not overhead

What This Role Is Not

- Not a solo-operator role - if your best work happens when nobody sees it until it's done, this will be a bad fit
 - Not an ML research role
 - Not a role where AI tools are optional

Compensation & Logistics

Compensation based on experience. Standard options package per company policy. 

Target start: Immediately

Final Note

We will go deep into your past work - what you built, why you built it that way, what broke, and who else could run it after you. The engineers who thrive here are the ones whose systems outlive their attention: documented, reviewed, and understood by the team. 

Bold Business - AI-First. Delivery-First. Team-First.

data.title: SDE II, EE Experiences, Progressive Discovery and Monetization
data.description:
Description

Everyday Essentials (EE) is a $100B+ business and one of the fastest-growing categories at Amazon - the household staples, health and personal care, grocery, and beauty products hundreds of millions of customers reorder. We're reinventing how customers discover, buy, and get more value from them, and we're looking for Software Development Engineers who want to build that future. 

The EE Experiences organization builds the shopping experience for the products customers come back for most. Our charter is Progressive Discovery and Monetization: helping customers find better products for their needs, complete their baskets, and improve EE business economics - and giving the world's largest consumer brands new and effective ways to reach those customers and grow with Amazon. We build a durable, profitable business at the intersection of the two, on the surfaces customers use every day. 

This is a space where the hardest problems don't have off-the-shelf answers. We're not polishing a solved product - we're inventing experiences that don't exist yet, and the decisions we make now shape a business with room to grow for years. You'll build discovery and recommendation features, brand-facing advertising surfaces, and the backend services that power them. Your work moves from whiteboard to production in front of a very large customer base, with visibility all the way to senior leadership. 

We're an AI-first team, and that shows up in two ways. We use AI throughout how we build software, and we expect our engineers to keep learning and applying the latest tools to move faster and raise the quality bar. AI is also at the core of what we build - the intelligence that helps customers find the right product is a modeling and engineering problem we work on hand in hand with scientists. If you're curious about AI, learn quickly, and like using it to solve real customer problems while keeping a clear head about where it helps and where it doesn't, you'll fit right in. 

Key job responsibilities

Design, build, and own software end to end - from customer research through design, code, testing, deployment, and production operations. 

Take on ambiguous problems where the goal is clear but the path is not, bring clarity, and deliver simple solutions that improve how customers find and buy everyday essentials. 

Partner closely with scientists, product managers, and designers to turn customer and brand problems into products that ship worldwide. 

Use generative AI tools and modern engineering practices to raise quality and velocity, and coach teammates on getting the most from them. 

Own operational health for your services - monitor metrics, drive root-cause fixes, and keep improving the experience for customers and brand partners. 

Raise the technical bar through code reviews, mentoring, and hiring for the best talent. 

A day in the life

Most days start with the customer problem in front of you: how to help someone find better everyday-essentials products faster, or how to give brands a more effective way to reach shoppers or how to improve the profitability of the business. You dig into data, sketch a design, and talk it through with product managers and scientists before writing any code. By the afternoon you might be prototyping an idea that didn't exist yesterday, reviewing a teammate's change, or debugging something in production. Because so much here is new, you won't just pick up tickets. You'll help decide what to build, push for the approach you believe in, and see your work reach customers in weeks, not quarters. 

About The Team

Our team owns how customers discover and buy the everyday essentials they rely on - and how the brands behind those products reach them. Our mission is to make restocking the things you need effortless, help customers find better options and to improve the business economics along the way. Day to day you'll work with fellow engineers and partner closely with product managers, designers, and scientists, who bring the customer and data insight that shapes what we build. We're a small, fast-moving group solving open-ended problems for hundreds of millions of shoppers - a place where you own problems end to end and your ideas reach customers fast.

 - 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience

data.title: Manager, Testing & Analysis Services
data.description:
About Prayoga

- Prayoga is a Bangalore-based research organisation working in science education and scientific research. Alongside this work, Prayoga offers analytical testing to external clients from its own laboratories. 
 - This role leads Prayoga's testing and analysis services end to end. 
 - The role
 - We are looking for an experienced testing-lab professional to own Prayoga's testing and analysis services, from the first client conversation to the signed test report. You will understand what clients need, run the labs and the technician team, and keep every test within an ISO/IEC 17025 (NABL) quality system. 
 - You will be technically strong in instrumental analysis, at ease with clients, and practised in running an accredited lab. Experience of taking a lab through NABL accreditation, or of leading its assessments, is a strong advantage. You will also help grow the testing service into a self-sustaining business. Key responsibilities

- Clients and business•  Be the technical front end for clients: understand their samples, purpose and regulatory needs, and recommend the right tests and methods. 

-     Review requests, tenders and contracts for technical feasibility, capacity and turnaround before accepting work. 
 - Prepare quotations, scopes of work and timelines with the finance team. 
 -     Communicate results and interpretations clearly, and handle client queries and complaints to closure. 
 -   Build repeat business and identify new testing services, sectors and partnerships. 
 - Laboratory operations
 -   Plan and run day-to-day lab work: sample receipt, registration, chain of custody, scheduling, testing and reporting. 
 - Own turnaround time, throughput and data integrity across all tests. 
 - Review and approve test reports; act as an authorised signatory once approved. 
 -   Manage instruments end to end: qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ), calibration, preventive maintenance, AMCs and vendor service. 
 - Manage consumables, reference standards, CRMs, reagents and inventory. 
 - Ensure lab safety, chemical handling, waste disposal and housekeeping. 
 - Quality system and NABL
 -     Implement and maintain a quality management system to ISO/IEC 17025: 2017 and NABL requirements. 
 -   Lead NABL accreditation, scope extension, surveillance and reassessment; prepare for and host assessments and close non-conformities. 
 - Develop, validate and verify test methods to national and international standards (BIS, ISO, ASTM, AOAC, USP/IP, EPA, FSSAI as relevant). 
 -   Estimate measurement uncertainty and maintain metrological traceability. 
 -     Plan proficiency testing and inter-laboratory comparisons, and act on the results. 
 -   Run internal audits, management reviews, CAPA, document control and records management. Team

-   Lead, recruit, train and assess technicians and analysts; maintain competence and authorisation records. 
 - Set daily priorities, review work and build a culture of accuracy, safety and ownership. 
 - Planning and reporting
 - Prepare the testing service's annual plan and budget, covering revenue, costs, capital equipment and staffing. 
 -   Report monthly to leadership on revenue, turnaround, quality indicators and client feedback. 
 - Advise on new instruments, capabilities and lab expansion. Qualifications and experience

- Essential

data.title: Performance Engineer
data.description:
A Performance Engineer specializing in LoadRunner is responsible for designing, executing, and analyzing performance, load, stress, and endurance tests for enterprise applications. [1, 2]

You can browse active openings on the Performance Testing Loadrunner Jobs on Naukri. com or reference a real-world enterprise profile like the Accenture Performance Engineer Position. [1, 2]

Key Job Description (JD) Structure

1. Role Summary / Objective

To ensure high application availability, scalability, and stability under peak traffic loads by building realistic virtual user scenarios, isolating bottlenecks, and collaborating with development and infrastructure teams. [1, 2, 3]

2. Must-Have Technical Skills

- Core LoadRunner Tools: Proficiency with VuGen (Virtual User Generator) for scripting, Controller / Performance Center / LoadRunner Enterprise (LRE) / LoadRunner Cloud for scenario execution, and LoadRunner Analysis for reporting. [1, 2]
 - Scripting & Protocols: Experience recording and enhancing scripts across protocols (HTTP/HTTPS, Web/HTML, REST/SOAP APIs, WebSockets, or TruClient). [1, 2, 3]
 - Script Enhancements: Hands-on skill in correlation (handling dynamic session IDs/tokens) and parameterization (using data pools for varied user input). [1, 2]
 - Alternative / Complementary Tools: Familiarity with JMeter, LoadNinja, or code-centric frameworks like DevWeb / LoadRunner Developer. [1, 2, 3]
 - Monitoring & APM Tools: Integration knowledge with Application Performance Monitoring tools like Dynatrace, AppDynamics, or Datadog to map slow SQL queries and server-side CPU/memory bottlenecks. [1]
 - Database & Querying: Basic SQL skills to validate backend database performance and data-intensive applications. [1]
 - Cloud & DevOps: Exposure to cloud environments (AWS, Azure) and CI/CD pipeline integration (Azure DevOps, Jenkins). [1]

3. Key Responsibilities

- Test Strategy & Design: Translate non-functional requirements (NFRs) into comprehensive performance test strategies and workload models. 
 - Script Development & Maintenance: Build, debug, and maintain reusable LoadRunner VuGen scripts for complex multi-step business transactions. 
 - Execution & Simulation: Execute load, stress, spike, and endurance (soak) tests using LoadRunner Controller or Cloud platforms. 
 - Diagnosis & Root Cause Analysis (RCA): Analyze graphs, run-time data, and APM metrics to pinpoint memory leaks, thread contention, network latency, or database locks. 
 - Reporting & Collaboration: Present performance test results, track defects in ALM/Jira/Azure DevOps, and work closely with developers to tune code and infrastructure. [1, 2, 3, 4]

4. Typical Qualifications & Experience

- Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field (typically 15 years of full-time education). [1]
 - Experience: 3 to 6+ years of dedicated experience in performance testing and engineering (often categorized as Senior Analyst or Engineer level). [1]
 - Domain Experience: Preferred background in high-transaction industries such as Banking, Financial Services, Capital Markets, or E-commerce. [1]

data.title: Lead Engineer – Mechanical (5–6 Years Experience)
data.description:
About the role: 

We are looking for a mechanically strong Lead Engineer - Mechanical with 5 to 6 years of experience to lead our product development team. You will own machine programmes end to end - from concept definition and hand calculations through detailed CAD models, engineering drawings, prototype builds, field validation, and release to production. Beyond your own design work, you will set the technical direction for the team, review and sign off the calculations and drawings of junior engineers, and be accountable for whether the design works in the field. You will be expected to think analytically, justify decisions with numbers, and iterate quickly based on real-world feedback. 

Roles and Responsibilities: 

- Own the mechanical design of complete agricultural machines and lead their development from concept through production release: structural frames, drive systems, conveyor mechanisms, cutting assemblies, and collection systems
 - Define design architecture and specifications at the concept stage - establish load cases, duty cycles, safety factors, and design targets before detailed work begins
 - Perform and review engineering calculations to size components and validate designs before fabrication: forces, torques, stresses, deflections, fatigue, and power requirements; act as the technical check on the team's calculation sheets
 - Develop 3D models and detailed manufacturing drawings using parametric CAD; apply GD&T for fabrication clarity, and review the models and drawings released by the team
 - Guide component selection - bearings, chains, sprockets, fasteners, seals, motors - using manufacturer catalogues and relevant IS / BS / ISO standards, and standardise part selection across machines
 - Mentor and technically supervise junior design engineers: allocate design work, run design reviews, and build the team's analytical discipline
 - Work directly with the fabrication workshop and external vendors to resolve manufacturing constraints, drive design for manufacture and cost, review first-article parts, and close the loop between drawing and metal
 - Plan and lead prototype testing in field conditions; define validation criteria, analyse failure modes, and drive design changes through to closure
 - Own the NPD documentation set - calculation sheets, design records, BOMs, and change control - and hold the team to it

What we are looking for: 

-   B. E. / B. Tech in Mechanical Engineering, M. Tech. in Engineering Design from a recognised institution
 - 5 to 6 years of experience in mechanical product design, machine design, or equipment engineering, including demonstrated ownership of at least one product or machine taken from concept to production
 - Experience guiding junior engineers and reviewing their design output, whether formally as a lead or informally within a project team
 - Strong analytical foundation in Engineering Mechanics (EM): ability to construct free body diagrams, analyse static and dynamic systems, resolve forces in mechanisms, and calculate power and torque through multi-stage drive trains
 - Strong analytical foundation in Strength of Materials (SOM): confident in stress and strain calculations, beam bending, torsional shear, column buckling, contact stress, and fatigue life estimation using standard criteria such as Goodman or Soderberg
 - Proficiency in Autodesk Inventor or equivalent parametric CAD; working proficiency in FEA simulation (ANSYS, or equivalent) with the judgement to know when a hand calculation is sufficient
 - Practical experience with fabrication processes and vendor interaction, and the ability to design for the equipment and skills actually available on the shop floor
 - Ability to read engineering standards and apply them practically to material selection, tolerancing, and component specification.

data.title: Quality Engineer AI First
data.description:
Quality Engineer (AI-first Testing)

About the role

You will be the first AI-first quality engineer at Verdantis, testing an AI-native platform MRO360 and our MDM product that large plants in energy, manufacturing and mining use to run their spare parts, equipment and material master data. The product makes decisions, not just screens: it recommends stock levels, flags duplicate materials and classifies parts. Testing means testing both the software and the judgement. 

We do not want a manual tester with a 400-row spreadsheet, nor a classic automation engineer maintaining brittle scripts. We want someone early in their career who already uses AI to generate test cases, write and repair automation, explore edge cases and read logs and who wants to find out how far that can go. You will set the pattern for how quality is done here. 

What you do

Functional testing

- Own test coverage for new features across MRO360 and MDM: read the story, generate the test cases with AI, prune and sharpen them yourself, and execute them before the sprint closes. 
 - Test the AI behavior, not just the UI: build evaluation sets for recommendations (stock levels, duplicate detection, classification), define what "correct" means with the product manager and data scientists, and track accuracy release over release. 
 - Reproduce customer-reported defects with real-shaped data (SAP material master, equipment, BOM extracts), write them up so a developer can fix them in one pass, and verify the fix. Platform testing

- Build and maintain automated regression suites (API and UI) written with AI, reviewed and owned by you that run on every build. 
 - Run integration tests against SAP-style data flows: flat-file loads, OData/IDoc payloads, error handling, idempotency on re-runs. 
 - Test what enterprise customers' security and IT teams will ask about: role-based access, multi-tenant data isolation, performance at 200K+ SKUs, audit logs. Raising the bar

- Keep a living record of which AI tools and prompts work for which testing tasks and share it with engineering, so test generation becomes part of how developers work. 
 - Report release readiness in one page the Engineering Lead and the Delivery Head can act on: what was tested, what was not, what is risky. 
 - Push back on shipping when the evidence says no. What we are looking for

- 1-3 years in software testing or development, or a strong fresher with projects that show it. Attitude and tooling fluency matter more than years. 
 - Uses AI tools daily and can show it: a test suite generated and refined with an LLM, an automation script debugged with Copilot or Claude, a prompt library built for test design. We will ask for a live demonstration. 
 - Can write code: Python or JavaScript/TypeScript well enough to build and repair automation (Playwright, Selenium, pytest, Postman/REST clients) without waiting for a developer. 
 - Knows the basics of good testing: boundary cases, equivalence classes, negative paths, test data design and can explain why an AI-generated test case is weak. 
 - Comfortable with SQL for checking data loads and results against the database. 
 - Curious about the domain: willing to learn what a material master, a reorder point or an equipment BOM is, because the bugs that matter are domain bugs. 
 - Writes a clear defect report and a clear release note. Argues with evidence, not opinion. 
 - Based in or willing to relocate to Mumbai. Nice to have

- Exposure to testing LLM-based features: prompt regression, evaluation datasets, hallucination and consistency checks. 
 - Experience with CI pipelines (GitHub Actions or similar) and running tests in them. 
 - Basic understanding of cloud deployments and multi-tenant SaaS. 
 - Any exposure to SAP, EAM or supply chain software is useful, not required. 
 - Performance or load testing with k6, JMeter or Locust. Who this role is not for

- Someone who wants a test plan handed to them and executes it line by line. 
 - Someone who sees AI as a shortcut to avoid understanding the product. The tool generates; you are accountable. 
 - Someone who wants to stay in one layer. This role spans UI, API, data and model behaviour. 
 - Someone who is uncomfortable telling a senior developer their feature is not ready.

data.title: General Manager - Central Quality
data.description:
General Manager - Central Quality

Location: Bengaluru, Karnataka

Experience: 2-4 Years

Department: Central Manufacturing

Reporting To: Head of Manufacturing

About Native

Native is Urban Company's in-house consumer products brand. Urban Company, founded in 2014, is Asia's largest technology marketplace for home services, and Native builds smart home products around problems we have seen first-hand while serving millions of homes. 

Native was born out of our service business. After servicing more than a million water purifiers and completing over 100, 000 carpentry jobs, we understood where existing products fail and how Indian homes are actually built. In 2023 we turned those insights into products: Native smart door locks, followed by a range of smart RO water purifiers. 

Every Native product is backed by the Urban Company platform. Customers buy through the Urban Company app, our trained professionals install the product, and our after-sales network services it. That closed loop gives our engineers direct insight into how products perform in real homes. 

Our innovations include: 

• Service-free water purification - India's first purifiers that need no servicing for 2 years, and the Native M3 Pro, with long-life filtration of up to 3 years and a 3-year unconditional warranty. 

• Connected product health - Customers track water TDS, filter health and consumption through the Urban Company app. 

• Locks designed for Indian homes - Designed to fit the vast majority of Indian doors, with reversible handles, doorbell-connected activation with visitor photos (Lock Pro), and face unlock (Lock Ultra). 

• More on the way

About the Role

We are looking for a hands-on Quality Control Engineer to anchor quality across our product lifecycle - from supplier inputs to field performance. You will own process control, spec documentation, supplier audits, NPI quality gates, and field issue resolution as a central function bridging design, manufacturing, and supply chain teams. 

You will also analyse field failures - facilitating RCA with lab teams to get to the root cause, enhancing IQC processes based on the learnings, and tracking the improvement in field failure rates that comes from more stringent IQC. 

Key Responsibilities

Process Control

- Define, monitor, and maintain Statistical Process Control (SPC) parameters for critical manufacturing operations
 - Own and update Control Plans for all active product lines, including CTQ (Critical to Quality) characteristics
 - Conduct periodic process audits on the shop floor and flag deviations with structured CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Action)
 - Collaborate with production teams to embed quality checkpoints into assembly and testing stages

Supplier Quality Control

- Conduct Incoming Quality Control (IQC) for raw materials and bought-out components against approved specs
 - Perform supplier audits and maintain supplier scorecards for on-time quality compliance
 - Drive PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) or equivalent first-article approvals for new or changed components
 - Raise and track Supplier Corrective Action Reports (SCARs) and verify effectiveness of closures

Specification & Ideal Spec Documentation

- Create and maintain Ideal Spec Sheets, tolerance documents, and inspection criteria for components and finished goods
 - Standardize Acceptance Quality Limits (AQL) sampling plans aligned with IS/BIS or applicable standards
 - Maintain a centralized spec repository and ensure version control across engineering change cycles
 - Author and update SOPs, Work Instructions, and quality checklists for inspection stations

Field Issue Resolution

- Act as the QC anchor for field complaints and warranty returns - triage, document, and drive root cause analysis
 - Use structured tools such as 8D, Fishbone (Ishikawa), and 5-Why for failure investigation and reporting
 - Coordinate with service, design, and production teams to close issues with verified corrective actions
 - Track field failure rate trends and proactively flag systemic issues to product and engineering teams

New Product Introduction (NPI)

- Participate in Design for Quality (DFQ) reviews during NPI stages - provide quality risk assessments
 - Define and execute First Article Inspection (FAI) and pilot batch qualification protocols
 - Establish quality benchmarks, test plans, and inspection checklists before production scale-up
 - Ensure all NPI components and assemblies have approved specs and supplier qualifications before launch

Qualifications & Skills Area Requirement

- Education - B. E. /B. Tech in Mechanical, Electrical, or Industrial Engineering
 - Experience - 3 years in a QC/QA role in a manufacturing environment
 - Standards Knowledge - IS/BIS, ISO 9001, AQL sampling (IS 2500)
 - Tools - SPC, CAPA, 8D, FMEA, PPAP/FAI
 - Software - MS Excel (data analysis), QMS tools, basic ERP/PLM familiarity
 - Soft Skills - Cross-functional communication, structured problem-solving, documentation discipline

What Sets a Strong Candidate Apart for Us

- Experience in electromechanical product quality (pumps, appliances, or similar assemblies)
 - Exposure to multilevel BOM-based quality control - component level through finished goods
 - Ability to write clear, copy-paste-ready spec and test documents independently
 - Demonstrated ownership of at least one full NPI cycle from pilot to production

KPIs for This Role

- Incoming rejection rate (%) by supplier
 - Field complaint closure time (days)
 - NPI first-pass qualification success rate
 - Supplier SCAR closure rate within target timelines
 - Control plan and spec documentation coverage (%)

data.title: QA Engineer (WFO)
data.description:
QA Engineer

Key Responsibilities

- Own whether the platform is safe to release - the automated suite, the manual passes automation cannot replace, and the judgement about what a failing test actually means
 - Build and keep the end-to-end suite in Playwright across the journeys that matter - a patient booked, registered, seen, billed, dispensed to and reported on - and keep it fast and trustworthy enough that nobody is tempted to ignore a red build
 - Write the test plan for each module from what the hospital does rather than from what the screen shows, with the Business Analyst and the module owner in the room
 - Own the regression pack that runs before every release, and grow it every time something escapes
 - Run beta: put each release in front of the hospital's own people on migrated data, log what they find so it can be reproduced, and close it before the next release starts
 - Be the person who says a release is not ready, and be right often enough that it carries weight

Where Testing Is Mandatory

- Money - every path that produces a bill, a discount, a refund or a day-end total, including the ones that fail halfway through
 - Stock - batch, expiry, issue and return, and the concurrent case where two counters sell the last strip
 - Clinical safety - allergy and interaction checks, dose limits by age and weight, critical values, and every alert that must reach a human
 - Access - that one hospital cannot see another's data, and that a role cannot do what it should not
 - Integrations - a laboratory result from a real analyser, an image from a real modality, an ABHA created against the real sandbox; a mock proves the code, not the hospital
 - Test the failure paths as seriously as the happy ones; the happy path is the one everybody already tried

Beta, Parallel Run and Go-Live

- Turn the acceptance scripts into something the hospital's own staff can run and sign, on their own migrated data, in the beta environment
 - Design the parallel run: what is entered in both systems, what is reconciled daily, and what "the numbers match" means for registrations, bills, collections, dispensing and reports
 - Be on the floor through cutover and hypercare, where the real testing happens, and bring what you see back into the suite
 - Own test data: realistic, safe, and reproducible, including the awkward records that break things - the duplicate patient, the expired batch, the refund after a partial payment

Working With the Team

- Sit in on specification work early, because the cheapest defect is the one caught while the specification is still a paragraph
 - Keep every defect described so that someone who was not there can reproduce it - steps, data, environment, what was expected, what happened
 - Track what escaped and why, and bring it to the retrospective rather than to an individual
 - Pair with engineers on the automated checks that live beside the code, so testing is not a gate at the end but a habit along the way

Tech Stack

Playwright

- TypeScript
 - pytest
 - Python
 - FastAPI
 - PostgreSQL
 - SQL
 - REST
 - OpenAPI
 - GitHub Actions
 - Docker
 - HL7 v2
 - FHIR
 - ABDM

We build in Python on FastAPI with React in front of it, on Amazon Web Services, and we test it with Playwright and pytest. That is what this role writes, runs and reads every day, and we would rather say it plainly at the top than have you find out in week one. 

What you will work in every day

- End-to-end testing - Playwright with TypeScript, against the real web application: journeys, fixtures, test data builders, and traces that say why a run failed
 - API and service testing - pytest and pytest-asyncio against FastAPI services; the OpenAPI schema is the contract, and tests are written to it
 - Database verification - PostgreSQL and SQL good enough to prove in the database what the screen claims, and to spot the migration that silently rounded a rupee
 - Continuous integration - GitHub Actions; the suite runs on every pull request, and a red build blocks a merge
 - Environments - Docker-based environments for development, beta and UAT, each with its own reproducible data set
 - Performance - load testing at peak outpatient volume with k6 or Locust, and the judgement to know which number matters
 - Integration test beds - HL7 v2 messages from analysers over MLLP, DICOM modality worklist and PACS, and the ABDM sandbox for ABHA creation and consent
 - Defect and test management - a shared tracker visible to the hospital, with a published severity and response standard

What we need you to have used in production

- Playwright, Cypress or Selenium on a system people depended on - writing maintainable tests, not recording brittle ones
 - A programming language, enough to write helpers, fixtures and data builders; TypeScript or Python, and the other within the first month
 - API testing at the service layer, and the sense to know which layer a case belongs at
 - SQL to verify data directly, not only through the screen
 - A CI pipeline your tests ran in, where a failure meant something to the team

Good to have as well

- Healthcare, banking, insurance, or another domain where a wrong number is a real consequence
 - Testing integrations with devices or external systems - an analyser, a payment gateway, a government API
 - Test design beyond the checklist: boundaries, equivalence classes, state transitions, concurrency
 - Accessibility and usability testing on screens used by people who did not choose the software
 - Running a user acceptance test with non-technical staff, and getting it signed
 - Security testing basics - role-based access, injection, the OWASP top ten - and reading a VAPT report

What You'll Bring

- Three or more years in software quality with real ownership of automation, not only manual execution
 - Have been the person who said a release was not ready, and can describe what you saw and what happened next
 - Enough programming to be useful in a codebase: helpers, fixtures, test data, and the occasional fix to the thing you found
 - Comfortable at the service layer and in the database, not only at the screen
 - Can write a defect report that a developer reproduces first time, and a test plan that a module owner recognises as their own work
 - Methodical about the awkward cases - the refund after a partial payment, the expired batch, the patient registered twice - because those are where a hospital gets hurt
 - Willing to sit at a billing counter or beside a nurse for a shift and come back with the cases the specification missed
 - Preferred: healthcare or another domain where correctness is auditable after the fact, and experience with a parallel run or a system cutover
